title: AI Medical Interpreter Pilot: 30-Day Scorecard
summary: Plan a 30-day AI medical interpreter pilot with baselines, quality metrics, teach-back, pause triggers, costs, and decision criteria.
body_markdown:
###


A 30-day pilot should decide whether a defined AI interpretation workflow is ready to continue, expand, narrow, or stop in the tested languages, sites, and encounter conditions. The decision should use preapproved measures for communication quality, patient understanding, access, workflow reliability, privacy readiness, and cost.


###


The most useful pilot metrics are clinically meaningful issues per reviewed encounter, teach-back results, successful escalation, time to usable interpretation, failed connections, eligible-encounter adoption, clinician effort, and cost per completed interpreted encounter. Report each metric by language and workflow instead of relying only on an overall average.


###


No. A completed escalation can show that the safety and patient-choice process worked as designed. Track the reason, time to resumed communication, completion status, language, and workflow separately for patient requests, technical problems, policy-based handoffs, and unresolved interpretation concerns.


###


There is no universal sample size for a 30-day pilot. The organization should choose a sample that reflects its languages, dialects, directions of interpretation, clinical tasks, shifts, and sites, and should report uncertainty and missing data. Low-volume languages may require a longer evaluation period before a decision is supportable.


###


No. A successful pilot supports decisions only within the tested languages, populations, workflows, devices, and conditions. Expansion should remain staged, with ongoing monitoring, patient choice, language-specific review, and a documented path to a qualified human interpreter when needed.
